Megan Thee Stallion has announced that she will depart the Broadway production of Moulin Rouge! The Musical ahead of schedule.

The 31-year-old rapper’s final show will now be this Friday, May 1.

In a statement to The Independent, she said: “Unfortunately, my last performance on Moulin Rouge! The Musical will be May 1. It’s been such an honor to be part of Moulin Rouge and I’ve met so many amazing people in this theater!

“Y’all work so hard and I have so much respect for the dedication, the stamina, the work ethic, the time and the effort y’all put into the work! Every single person at the Moulin Rouge has inspired me to go harder as an entertainer.

“I’m so grateful for the cast and crew that made this experience so meaningful. Y’all are really some of the kindest human beings I’ve ever met! To all the Hotties that showed up or planned to attend, thank you for supporting me during this incredible journey!”

open image in gallery Megan Thee Stallion onstage in ‘Moulin Rouge! The Musical’ ( Getty )

The news comes days after Megan Thee Stallion broke down in tears on stage hours after announcing her split from boyfriend Klay Thompson.

On Saturday (25 April), the “WAP” rapper posted on Instagram Stories, where she alleged that basketball player Thompson, 36, had cheated on her. He has not yet responded to the allegations.

In a statement to The Independent, Megan then confirmed that she and Thompson had split after less than a year of dating.

Just hours after announcing their split, Megan was back on stage, performing in the role of ringmaster Zidler in the hit Broadway musical. Megan joined the Tony-winning production in late March for an eight-week stint.

In a clip shared on TikTok, the musician could be seen turning away from the audience to wipe away her tears during the curtain call, with the show’s performers standing behind her and cheering her on.

Megan – whose full name is Megan Pete – gathered herself, wiping her tears from her hands before taking a bow.

It’s the second blow Megan has faced during her run in the show, after she was rushed to hospital mid-way through a performance in late March.

Megan subsequently cancelled two shows and wrote on social media that it had been “a real wake-up call for me”. “I’ve been pushing myself past my limits lately, running on empty, and my body finally said enough,” she said.

open image in gallery Klay Thompson during an NBA game with the Dallas Mavericks ( AP )

The rapper, who returned to the stage after two shows, first hinted at her split from Dallas Mavericks player Thompson on Saturday, when she shared a text-only post to Instagram claiming that he had been unfaithful.

“Cheating, had me around your whole family playing house…got ‘cold feet,’” she wrote.

“Holding you down through all your HORRIBLE mood swings and treatment towards me during your basketball season now you don’t know if you can be ‘monogamous’??? B**** I need a REAL break after this one…bye y’all.”

The split was then confirmed in a statement to The Independent, with Megan saying: “I’ve made the decision to end my relationship with Klay.

“Trust, fidelity and respect are non-negotiable for me in a relationship, and when those values are compromised, there’s no real path forward. I’m taking this time to prioritise myself and move ahead with peace and clarity.”

The pair began dating in spring 2025 and confirmed their relationship at a red carpet event in July 2025. Speaking at the time, Megan called the NBA star “the nicest person I’ve ever met in my life”.

News.title: Carrick deserves full-time job after guiding Man Utd to brink of Champions League
News.content:
The Premier League weekend comes to a close at Old Trafford as Manchester United host Brentford. The reverse fixture was won by Brentford 3-1 at the Gtech Stadium back in September. Brentford raced into a 2-0 lead thanks to Igor Thiago’s double before Benjamin Sesko got a goal back for Manchester United, who then missed a penalty in the second half before Mathias Jensen secured the three points for Brentford in second half stoppage time. If Brentford were to win this evening, it would be their first league double over Manchester United since 1936/37.

Manchester United claimed an important victory away at Chelsea last time out as they look to return to the Champions League. They start the night in third, ahead of Liverpool on goals scored and Aston Villa on goal difference. A win tonight would put them on the verge of Champions League qualification.

“I have said it many times, I enjoy being here, I enjoy the role I am in,” Michael Carrick said. “We have had some good results, and we are in decent shape. There is a lot to go. We still want to keep improving. There are layers that we want to get to really. I will see. I keep saying the same things in front of you every week. There is only so much I can say in terms of that, but I have said it many times again. I enjoy being here. I love being here. It is a real privilege to be in the position I am, but thriving with the responsibility that we got. I am not sure to be honest [when he will get clarity on his future] and it is not something in terms of deadlines that I am really chasing. I think it will become clear when it is going to become clear, and I am here at the moment to help the team and help the club get results. And at the moment, we are doing all right. We can still keep pushing and getting better. So really, that is genuinely all I am focused on.”

Lisandro Martinez is still suspended but Harry Maguire returns from his ban. Leny Yoro could return having missed the win at Chelsea whilst Matthijs de Ligt is closing in on a return from a long-term back problem.

Brentford have drawn their last five league games, including three goalless stalemates. The visitors go into this game in ninth but would rise into sixth with a victory at Old Trafford this evening.

News.title: Merz: Iran has humiliated Trump
News.content:
Friedrich Merz said the US had been humiliated by Iran, in an overt attack on Donald Trump.

The German chancellor also claimed that Washington “quite obviously went into this war without any strategy”, and said the Iranian leadership had been “negotiating very skilfully”.

Mr Merz said: “The Iranians are clearly stronger than expected and the Americans clearly have no truly convincing strategy in the negotiations either. The problem with conflicts like this is always: you don’t just have to get in, you have to get out again.

“We saw that very painfully in Afghanistan for 20 years. We saw it in Iraq. A whole nation is being humiliated by the Iranian leadership, especially by these so-called Revolutionary Guards.”

Mr Merz reiterated his offer to deploy German minesweepers to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but his attack will probably heighten already strained tensions between the US and Europe.

Iran wants to postpone nuclear talks

The reopening of the strait is one of the key stumbling blocks in negotiations to secure a peace deal between Iran and the US.

On Monday, Axios reported that Iran had submitted a new peace proposal to the US, in which it offered to open the key waterway while postponing talks on its nuclear programme.

Iran’s nuclear ambitions have been a major point of contention in negotiations between the two sides, but Tehran hopes the war can end without an agreement on its stockpile of enriched uranium.

The offer, conveyed via Pakistani mediators, reflects deep divisions in Iran over how far it is willing to go in meeting Washington’s demands. It also signals a shift towards securing immediate economic and military relief before tackling longer-term nuclear concessions.

Two US officials confirmed to Axios that the Trump administration had received the proposal, but Washington had made no decision on it. The White House is quoted as saying: “These are sensitive diplomatic discussions and the US will not negotiate through the press.”

Trump: ‘They cannot have a nuclear weapon’

Karoline Leavitt, the White House press secretary, said Donald Trump had discussed the Iranian proposal with his top national security aides on Monday.

On Sunday, Mr Trump insisted that a commitment to non-nuclear proliferation by Iran was a red line. He told Fox News: “They know what has to be in the agreement. It’s very simple: they cannot have a nuclear weapon. Otherwise there’s no reason to meet.”

Abbas Araghchi, the Iranian foreign minister, met Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg on Monday and they discussed efforts to end the war.

Mr Araghchi said the Islamic Republic was “stable, solid” during their talks, and claimed: “The world has now realised Iran’s true power.” He added that Russia had stood by Iran and the two countries would continue their “strategic partnership”.

News.title: Rubella (German Measles)
News.content:
Key facts

Rubella, also known as German measles, is a contagious illness caused by a virus

The main symptom of rubella is a spotty rash that starts on the face or neck and spreads to the rest of the body.

Rubella is usually a mild illness that gets better in about a week, but it can be serious for pregnant women

The measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine is effective in preventing the disease

Rubella is most often seen during the late winter and spring.

Overview

Rubella is a contagious disease caused by a virus. It is also known as German measles or three-day measles, although it is not related to measles. Although it is usually a mild illness that gets better within a week, it can be dangerous for pregnant women and there are thought to be about 100,000 cases of congenital rubella syndrome every year. Rubella is easily spread through coughs and sneezes.

Rubella is preventable through vaccination. The MMR vaccine is given to children in the UK in two doses and can give lifelong protection against all three diseases. A single dose of the rubella vaccine provides more than 95 per cent long-lasting immunity.

Signs and symptoms

The main symptom of rubella is a spotty rash. The rash typically starts on the face or behind the ears, and then spreads to the neck and body. It can be red or pink on white skin and may be more difficult to see on brown or black skin, although it might feel rough or bumpy. The rash usually appears two to three weeks after getting infected. However, in up to 50 per cent cases there is no rash.

Other symptoms of rubella can include:

Aching fingers, wrists, or knees

A high temperature

Coughs

Sneezing and a runny nose

Headaches

A sore throat

Sore, red eyes

Swollen glands in the neck or behind the ears.

Dangers and complications

Rubella can be particularly dangerous for pregnant women. If a pregnant woman contracts rubella, it can lead to miscarriage or birth defects in the baby, known as congenital rubella syndrome. There are an estimated 100,000 cases of this every year. Problems can include issues with the baby’s sight, hearing, hear, or brain. The risk is highest if the woman contracts rubella early in the pregnancy. Before the introduction of the rubella vaccine, an estimated four babies in every 1,000 globally were born with the condition.

Transmission

Rubella is spread through coughs and sneezes and is most prevalent during winter and early spring. To avoid spreading the disease, infected people should stay off nursery, school, or work for seven days after the rash appears.

Treatment

There is no specific treatment for rubella. The illness usually gets better in about a week with rest and plenty of fluids. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can be taken to relieve discomfort, but aspirin should not be given to children under 16. The NHS recommends you should call your GP for advice rather than going to the surgery and spreading the disease to others.

Prevention

The MMR vaccine is highly effective and provides lifelong protection against measles, mumps, and rubella. Two doses of the vaccine are recommended. Women who plan to become pregnant but do not have sufficient levels of antibodies to the virus can get a rubella-containing vaccine 28 days before conception.

History

Rubella was first described in 1740 by German physician and chemist Friedrich Hoffman as causing distinctive reddish-pink marks. It was given the name German measles, and also known as ‘Röteln’ which means “reddish” or “pink” in German. However, rubella and measles are not related. In 1866, Henry Veale, an English Royal Artillery surgeon, coined the name “rubella” (from the Latin word meaning “little red”) when he described an outbreak in India.

The rubella virus was isolated in 1962 and work on a vaccine began in earnest after the last major rubella epidemic in the United States from 1964 to 1965, when an estimated 12.5 million people got the disease, 11,000 pregnant women lost their babies, 2,100 newborns died, and 20,000 babies were born with congenital rubella syndrome.

The first vaccines were introduced in 1969 and in 1970 in the UK a vaccination programme for girls was introduced. The first combined MMR vaccine was introduced in the UK in 1988.

Reported rubella cases have plummeted since more countries introduced vaccine programmes from 670,894 cases in 102 countries in 2000 to 17,865 cases in 78 countries in 2022.

gavi.org/rubella

cdc.gov/rubella

News.title: Biological attack
News.content:
Key facts

Biological weapons use microorganisms like virus, bacteria or fungi to spread disease

Agents such as anthrax, botulinum toxin and plague could pose a huge public health threat, killing large numbers of people

A biological attack could be confused with a natural outbreak of disease, hampering the response and control

There are fears that pathogens could be modified to become deadlier or more transmissible

Overview

Biological weapons spread infectious agents or toxins to kill humans, animals or plants or contaminate a country’s food and/or water supply. They can be deadly and highly dangerous and spread beyond a country’s borders, making them difficult to control.

While infectious agents have long been used in wartime there are concerns that scientific advances – such as CRISPR gene editing tools and gain-of-function research – could be used by malign actors to modify pathogens to make them even more deadly and transmissible.

The toxin or infectious agent needs to be “weaponised” to be delivered to the target population. According to the United Nations previous bio-weapons programmes have seen the construction of missiles, bombs and hand grenades as a dirty bomb delivery method. Spray tanks have also been designed for vehicles and there have even been efforts to contaminate clothing.

While there are concerns about what could happen if terror groups get hold of bioweapons, many security experts believe that producing them requires a level of sophistication only available to national governments and state-sponsored groups.

Perhaps their greatest power lies in the power they hold in the collective imagination – in a letter to the BMJ in 2001 in the wake of anthrax attacks in the United States psychiatrists from the UK, US and Australia said the (understandable) panic the weapons evoke could cause more harm than the actual weapons themselves.

“The purpose of these weapons is to wreak destruction via psychological means – by inducing fear, confusion and uncertainty in everyday life,” they wrote.

Prevention

The United Nations Biological Weapons Convention came into force in 1975 and it forbids states from developing, producing, stockpiling, or sharing biological agents, toxins and equipment that have no justification for peaceful or defence purposes.

Some 184 countries have fully signed up to the treaty – however, in 2024 the United States government State Department raised concerns about the compliance of China, Iran, Russia and North Korea, all of which are full signatories.

Under the treaty countries can lodge a complaint with the UN Security Council if they believe other member states are violating the convention. The Security Council can investigate complaints, but this power has never been invoked.

History

The use of biological weapons is as old as warfare itself with reports of armies poisoning wells as far back as 600 BC. During the siege of Caffa (a town in modern-day Ukraine) in the 14th century the attacking Tartar forces experienced an outbreak of plague and threw the bodies of their dead comrades over the walls of the town to spread the disease. In 1797 Napoleon flooded the plains around the Italian town of Mantua to start a malaria epidemic.

During the First World War the Germans denied shipping cattle infected with anthrax to the United States and other countries, although its use of chemical weapons in the form of mustard gas is well documented. This led to the first international chemical and biological weapons treaty in 1925. However, during the Second World War many countries, including Britain, conducted bioweapon experiments.

Eventually a bioweapons treaty was signed in 1975, although western governments believe the Soviet Union continued a research programme for many years. In 1979 reports emerged of an anthrax outbreak in Sverdlovsk, near a military facility. The official version of events was that people had died after eating infected meat, however in 1992 the Russian president, Boris Yeltsin, admitted that the outbreak was caused by an accidental release of anthrax spores from a bioweapons facility.

In the 1990s the Aum Shinrikyo cult attacked the Tokyo subway with sarin gas, killing 13 people. Before this they had made three unsuccessful attempts at attacks with anthrax and botulinum toxin. Members had also tried to get hold of Ebola virus.

In 2001 – a week after the 9/11 terrorist attack – letters containing anthrax spores were sent to media organisations and two senators, killing five people. After a long investigation a scientist at the US government biodefence lab in Fort Detrick, Maryland, became the prime suspect but he committed suicide before he could be charged.

Useful links

who.int/health-topics/biological-weapons

disarmament.unoda.org/biological-weapons

News.title: Rotavirus
News.content:
Key facts

Rotavirus is a common infection that causes diarrhoea and vomiting, especially in babies and young children

The rotavirus vaccine is the best way to protect against rotavirus disease

Rotavirus is an RNA virus that is shed in the faeces of infected people

Symptoms of rotavirus include watery diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, and stomach pain

Overview

Rotavirus is a highly contagious virus that commonly causes severe watery diarrhoea and vomiting, particularly in infants and young children. Although most children recover within a few days, some may experience severe dehydration requiring hospital treatment. In very rare cases, rotavirus can be life-threatening. Globally, rotaviruses are the leading cause of severe diarrhoea in young children although the number of deaths has dropped since a vaccine became available.

Signs and symptoms

Symptoms of rotavirus typically begin up to three days after exposure and usually clear up within a week. However, symptoms can last up to two to three weeks.

The most common symptoms include:

Severe watery diarrhoea

Vomiting

Fever

Stomach pain

Additional symptoms can include loss of appetite and dehydration, which can be particularly dangerous for very young children. Signs of dehydration include decreased urination, dry mouth and throat, dizziness when standing, crying with few or no tears, and unusual sleepiness.

Dangers and complications

Rotavirus can lead to significant health risks, particularly due to the potential for severe dehydration, which dangerous for young children. Severe dehydration is treated with intravenous fluids. In some instances, if treatment is delayed, it can result in death. In poorer countries around 2.5 per cent of children who present to health facilities will die.

If a young child has had diarrhoea for more than 24 hours or their faeces is black and/or has blood in it you should take them to a doctor immediately.

Transmission

Rotavirus is primarily transmitted through contact with the faeces of infected individuals. The virus can easily spread in families, hospitals, and childcare centres. Transmission occurs when virus particles enter the mouth via unwashed hands, by touching contaminated objects or surfaces, or by eating contaminated food. People are most contagious when they have symptoms and during the first three days after recovery. They can also spread the virus before they develop symptoms. Rotavirus infections often follow a seasonal pattern, peaking in the winter and spring in countries with temperate climates.

Rotavirus is prevalent globally and, unlike bacterial diarrhoea, it is not linked to poor sanitation and hygiene. It is thought every child will have had it by their fifth birthday.

Treatment

There is no specific medicine to treat rotavirus infection, but your doctor may recommend medicine to treat the symptoms. Antibiotics are not effective against viruses such as rotavirus. The main treatment focuses on managing symptoms and preventing dehydration through oral rehydration therapy, which involves drinking a beverage containing water, sugar, and electrolytes. If dehydration is severe, hospitalisation for intravenous fluids may be required.

Prevention

The most effective way to prevent rotavirus disease is through vaccination. The rotavirus vaccine is part of routine immunisation programmes. In the UK, babies receive two doses of the vaccine at 8 and 12 weeks old. Additionally, practising good hygiene, such as frequent handwashing, is important in reducing the spread of the virus, alongside keeping children and young babies away from school and nursery when they are sick. While the vaccine doesn’t provide complete protection from infection, vaccinated children are less likely to become seriously unwell.

There is also a very small risk – one in 20,000 to one in 100,000 – of a serious problem where the bowel becomes blocked (intussusception) in the week after being vaccinated.

History

Rotavirus was first discovered in 1973 by an Australian team led by Ruth Bishop, who identified the wheel-shaped virus from intestinal biopsies of children with gastroenteritis. By 1980, rotavirus was recognised as the most common cause of severe gastroenteritis in infants and young children in the United States. In the prevaccine era, the was responsible for up to 500,000 deaths among children annually worldwide.

In 1998 the first rotavirus vaccine, RotaShield,was licenced in the United States but was withdrawn over the risk of blocked bowel. In 2005 two new vaccines were introduced and, alongside two additional vaccines, they are now used in more than 100 countries worldwide. Together they have contributed to marked decreases in hospitalisations and deaths from diarrhoea.

The rotavirus vaccine was introduced into the routine UK vaccination schedule in 2013. A study in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2016 found that the number of young children being admitted to hospital for acute gastroenteritis fell by 26 per cent the year after the introduction of the vaccine.

News.title: Polio
News.content:
Key facts

Polio is a serious infection caused by a virus.

It mainly affects children under 5 years of age.

The virus can cause paralysis, and in severe cases, death.

Polio is transmitted mainly through the faecal-oral route.

Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent polio.

Overview

Polio is caused by a virus that invades the nervous system and can cause paralysis within hours. There are three types of wild poliovirus with only type 1 still circulating. Although polio is now only endemic in Afghanistan and Pakistan, the potential threat from its continued circulation means that the World Health Organization (WHO) still classifies it as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

The Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) was launched in 1988, bringing together governments, donors, and health workers to raise awareness of the disease and improve access to polio vaccines. This has led to a 99 per cent reduction in polio cases, and an estimated 20 million children have been prevented from contracting polio since the GPEI was launched.

Signs and symptoms

Most people who contract polio do not have any symptoms. Some individuals develop mild, flu-like symptoms.

High temperature

Extreme tiredness (fatigue)

Headaches

Vomiting

Stiff neck

Muscle pain

These symptoms typically last up to 10 days. In rare cases, polio can lead to more serious symptoms affecting the brain and nerves, including muscle weakness and paralysis, typically in the legs.

Dangers and complications

Polio can lead to long-term or lifelong difficulties. If the paralysis affects the muscles used for breathing, it can be life-threatening. Some patients ended up in iron lungs – coffin like contraptions which helped them breathe. Some individuals may be left with permanent paralysis or other disabilities.

Complications can include:

Muscle weakness

Problems with joints

Swallowing difficulties (dysphagia)

Some people who have had polio may develop symptoms again or their symptoms may worsen, sometimes decades later, which is known as post-polio syndrome. This can cause muscle weakness that deteriorates over time, leading to pain and fatigue, and possibly disability.

Transmission

Polio is a highly infectious disease caused by a virus that spreads easily from person to person. It usually spreads through contact with the faeces of an infected person. This can happen by not washing hands properly and then putting them in the mouth, or through contaminated food or water. The virus multiplies in the intestine. It can also spread through coughs and sneezes, though this is less common. Polio is more common in areas where there is poor access to clean water and sanitation.

Treatment

There is no specific treatment for polio and care is supportive including:

Bed rest in hospital

Painkillers

Help with breathing

Regular stretches and exercises to prevent muscle and joint problems

Specialist help such as physiotherapy or surgery may be required if long-term problems arise from polio.

Prevention

The best way to prevent polio is through vaccination. The polio vaccine is part of the routine childhood vaccination schedule. In the UK, the polio vaccine is given to children at eight, 12, and 16 weeks old as part of the 6-in-1 vaccine, at 3 years, 4 months as part of the 4-in-1 pre-school booster, and at 14 years old as part of the teenage booster.

In addition to routine vaccinations, a polio booster may be required before travelling to certain countries. It’s essential to seek advice from a travel clinic, GP, nurse, or pharmacist before travelling abroad.

Washing hands with soap and water or using hand sanitiser regularly throughout the day also helps to avoid catching and spreading viruses.

History

Polio is an ancient disease, with evidence of sufferers depicted in ancient Egyptian engravings. The first clinical description of the disease was produced by British physician Michael Underwood in 1789. In 1840, Dr Jacob Von Heine, a German orthopaedic doctor, determined that poliomyelitis was a distinct disease and theorised that it had an infectious cause. The poliovirus that causes the disease was identified in 1909 by Austrian immunologist Karl Landsteiner.

Polio vaccines were introduced as routine immunisations in the 1970s, and the number of cases dropped dramatically. But by the late 1980s, polio was still paralysing over 1,000 children a day around the world. Since the launch of the GPEI in 1988 wild poliovirus cases have decreased by over 99 per cent. Type 2 wild poliovirus was declared eradicated in 2015, and type 3 was declared eradicated in October 2019. Type 1 remains in Afghanistan and Pakistan. The discovery of poliovirus in sewers in London demonstrated that the disease could still be a threat – the virus was thought to have been shed by someone visiting and endemic country and there were no active cases of the disease.

News.title: Pneumococcal Disease
News.content:
Key facts

Pneumococcal disease is caused by the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae

It is a major public health problem worldwide, especially for young children and the elderly

It is thought to kill about one million children every year, mainly in low and middle income countries

Pneumococcal bacteria can cause various infections, including pneumonia, meningitis, and ear infections

Vaccination is the best way to prevent pneumococcal disease

Overview

Pneumococcal disease refers to any infection caused by the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae, also known as pneumococcus. This bacterium lives in the nose and throat and can cause a range of infections, from mild illnesses like ear and sinus infections to serious conditions such as pneumonia and meningitis. Anyone can contract pneumococcal disease, but young children, the elderly, and people with compromised immunity are at higher risk.

There are around 90 different types of pneumococcus, although it is thought that only between eight and 10 of these are responsible for most cases of severe disease. The introduction of pneumococcal conjugate vaccines has greatly reduced the number of cases and deaths, but there are still millions of children who remain unvaccinated and vaccines do not protect against all strains.

Signs and symptoms

The symptoms of pneumococcal disease vary depending on the part of the body that is infected.

Common symptoms include:

a high temperature

chills

sweats

aches and pains

headache

a general sense of feeling unwell

earache

Other more serious symptoms include

Pneumonia: Cough, fever, chest pain, and breathing difficulties.

Meningitis: Fever, stiff neck, light sensitivity, headache, and confusion.

Bacteraemia: Fever, chills, and reduced alertness.

Dangers and complications

Pneumococcal infections can lead to severe complications. In low and middle-income countries, fatality rates for children with severe infections like bacteraemia or meningitis can range from 20 to 50 per cent.

Individuals with sickle cell disease, certain immune deficiencies, or chronic renal disease, and those taking immunosuppressive drugs are at an increased risk for pneumococcal infection. Smoking also increases the risk of the disease.

Transmission

Pneumococcal bacteria are transmitted through direct contact with respiratory secretions, such as saliva or mucus, from infected individuals. This can occur when an infected person coughs or sneezes, spreading droplets containing the bacteria. The risk of infection can vary by season, with higher rates during winter when people are more likely to be in close contact.

Treatment

Pneumococcal disease is treated with antibiotics. However, some strains of pneumococcus have developed resistance to certain antibiotics and testing is used to determine the most effective treatment.

Prevention

Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent pneumococcal disease. In the UK babies get their first dose at 16 weeks and a booster at a year old. Older adults also get a dose at the age of 65. Children and adults at a higher risk of the disease may also get an additional dose.

Simple infection control methods, such as covering your mouth and nose when you cough and sneeze and washing your hands regularly, particularly before preparing food, can also help prevent the spread of the disease.

History

Streptococcus pneumoniae has been causing disease and death for thousands of years but it was first isolated in France by Louis Pasteur in 1880 from the saliva of a patient with rabies. Researchers began developing a vaccine in South Africa in the 1920s but the first vaccine was not licenced until 1977. More advanced pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) were then developed and rolled out in the 2000s. They have since been expanded to protect against more strains of the disease.

A study in the Lancet estimated that in the 11 years after PCV was introduced into the UK schedule in 2006 it prevented around 40,000 cases of invasive pneumococcal disease, and about 2,000 deaths.

News.title: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
News.content:
Key facts

Pertussis, also known as whooping cough, is a highly contagious respiratory illness caused by the bacteria Bordetella pertussis

The illness begins with cold-like symptoms and a cough that worsens, sometimes resulting in violent coughing fits, and can last for weeks or months.

A characteristic “whoop” sound may occur when the affected person gasps for air between coughs

Whooping cough is most dangerous for babies

Vaccination is the best way to prevent whooping cough.

Overview

Whooping cough, or pertussis, is a respiratory infection that is highly contagious. It is caused by the bacterium Bordetella pertussis, and it is spread from person to person by coughing and sneezing. The disease can affect anyone but it is most dangerous for babies. Vaccination against pertussis is included in the UK’s routine immunisation schedule for babies.

Signs and symptoms

The first signs of whooping cough are similar to a cold, such as a runny nose and sore throat; a high temperature is uncommon. The cough associated with pertussis can last for weeks or months.

After about a week, the following symptoms may develop:

Coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night

A “whoop” sound, which is a gasp for breath between coughs (though young babies and some adults may not “whoop”)

Difficulty breathing after a coughing bout and possibly turning blue or grey (especially in young infants)

Bringing up thick mucus, which can cause vomiting

Becoming very red in the face (more common in adults)

The coughing episodes can be violent enough to trigger vomiting,

Dangers and complications

Babies under 12 months old with whooping cough have an increased chance of developing serious problems, such as dehydration, breathing difficulties, pneumonia, and seizures. Babies with whooping cough can temporarily stop breathing, turn blue, and experience seizures or brain damage, with roughly half of infected infants under one requiring hospital care.

While less severe in older children and adults, whooping cough can still cause problems such as sore ribs, hernia, middle ear infections and urinary incontinence. A severe cough can also lead to chest pain, which could indicate pneumonia.

Transmission

Whooping cough spreads easily from person to person through the air. When an infected person coughs or sneezes, they release small particles containing the bacteria, which others can then breathe in. This is more likely to happen when people spend a lot of time together or share breathing space.

People can spread the bacteria from the start of symptoms and for up to three weeks after the coughing begins. Some people may have mild symptoms and not know they have whooping cough, but can still spread the bacteria. Many babies who get whooping cough are infected by older siblings, parents, or caregivers who are unaware they have it.

Treatment

Treating whooping cough early with antibiotics may make the infection less serious. If diagnosed within two weeks of the cough starting, antibiotics can help stop it spreading to others, although they may not reduce symptoms.

Hospital treatment is usually needed for severe whooping cough or if it is in a young baby. To ease symptoms, get plenty of rest, drink fluids, and take paracetamol or ibuprofen if uncomfortable. Aspirin should not be given to children under 16.

Prevention

The best way to prevent whooping cough is through vaccination. The whooping cough vaccine is routinely given as part of the 6-in-1 vaccine for babies at eight, 12, and 16 weeks, and the 4-in-1 pre-school booster for children aged 3 years 4 months. Pregnant women are also advised to have the whooping cough vaccine, usually around 20 weeks of pregnancy, to help protect their baby for the first few weeks of life.

Preventive antibiotics, also known as postexposure antimicrobial prophylaxis, may be given to someone who has been exposed to the bacteria to prevent them from getting sick. It’s also recommended to practice good hygiene to prevent the spread of bacteria and viruses.

Although people who have had whooping cough have some immunity, it does not provide lifelong protection, and re-infection is possible.

History

The earliest medical descriptions of pertussis are thought to be from a Persian physician who described an outbreak of violent coughing in Rey (near present-day Tehran) in the late winter of 1501.

In the early 20th century, whooping cough was a common childhood disease and a major cause of childhood deaths – in the United States, for example, there were up to 200,000 cases reported annually.

In 1906 the bacterium was isolated, leading to the development of the first vaccine in 1913. A much more effective vaccine was developed in 1939, and in the late 1940s it was combined with diphtheria and tetanus to create a single jab and was rolled out widely. It was refined again in the 1980s.

The advent of vaccination has not seen the disease disappear completely. Pertussis is cyclical, with outbreaks every three to five years. The last big outbreak in the UK was in 2012, when there were over 9,300 cases in England alone – this was more than 10 times as many as in previous years – and 14 babies under three months old died.

After a historic low during the Covid pandemic, 2024 saw a resurgence of the disease globally – in England, between January and May 2024, there were 7,599 confirmed cases, with eight infant deaths over the same period. By contrast, there were just 858 cases reported during the whole of 2023.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes’ incredible Man Utd career in numbers as he matches Ronaldo tally and closes in on Premier League record
Sports.content:
FOR more than six years Manchester United have effectively been carried by one player, Bruno Fernandes.

The Red Devils have often lived and died by the Portuguese playmaker’s displays.





This season, which could yet be his last in the United shirt, Fernandes has been second to none and put in another stunning display against Brentford.

It was his corner which found Harry Maguire at the far post who nodded the ball back for Casemiro to score the opener.

Fernandes was on hand again to play in Benjamin Sesko for the clincher two minutes before the break as United scored a blistering counter-attack.

That assist moved the 31-year-old one behind the Premier League assist record of 20 held by Kevin De Bruyne and Thierry Henry – both achieved in far more functional Manchester City and Arsenal teams than what United can boast.



It also saw Fernandes become the first United player since Robin van Persie in 2012/13 to hit a goal or assist in seven consecutive Prem games.

With his latest goal contribution, Fernandes moved on to 140 top flight goal contributions for United – a perfect 70 goals and 70 assists split.

That is the same number as compatriot and club icon Cristiano Ronaldo, with 103 goals and 37 assists across his two stints in the North West of England.

Back in March, he overtook David Beckham’s United record of 15 for most assists in a single season set in the 1999/2000 campaign.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

In all comps his numbers are even more impressive, tallying up 106 goals and 106 assists in all competitions.

Fernandes is in the running for Premier League Player of the Year, Arsenal’s Declan Rice seemingly his main competition, as he continues to smash club and league records.

But he has the backing of Michael Carrick to be awarded that gong at the end of the season.

Speaking after the 2-1 win over Brentford, when asked if Fernandes merited the end-of-season awards, Carrick said: “Hopefully he does. He deserves it.

“For the impact that he’s had and the moments that he’s created. I think, whether that’s creating, whether that’s scoring.



“How his influence within the group is. He’s had a big season. There’s no getting away from it. And it was another good performance for him tonight.”

Bruno Fernandes' Man Utd career in numbers Bruno Fernandes' stats since he joined United in January 2020: Games: 323 Goals: 106 Assists: 106 Honours: FA Cup 2024, League Cup 2023 PFA Team of the Year: 2020/21 Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year: 2019/20, 2020/21, 2023/24, 2024/25

In a previous era at United, the talk would be of one of the all-time great Prem midfielders, with titles to boot.

However, United’s deficiencies on and off the pitch have meant the club are often far from competing at the table for football‘s top prizes.

For his part, since joining in January 2020, Fernandes could not have done much more to help the club win titles.



He came close to leaving the club last summer, but rejected a big offer of Saudi cash to be the centrepiece of the ill-fated Ruben-Amorim project.

But his performances both as a No6 in a deeper pivot role and back as a No10 under Carrick have been the heartbeat of United’s charge towards returning to the Champions League next season.

That should help the club attract the talent it needs to recruit in order to build a squad capable of a title challenge.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

With a crucial victory over Brentford on United’s sixth Monday game of the season, Fernandes and Co know beating Liverpool next Sunday will confirm Champions League football for next season.

That will likely end any and all speculation over his future, though United have already told their captain they do not want him leaving regardless, as SunSport exclusively revealed.

Sports.title: Man Utd boss Carrick issues strict demand to squad ahead of Liverpool clash as they near Champions League return
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK insists Manchester United should not “over-celebrate” their probable Champions League qualification.

United are two points away from mathematically securing a return to the premier club competition with four games remaining after beating Brentford 2-1.



Carrick’s side could be assured of a top five finish before kick-off against Liverpool on Sunday if Brighton lose at Newcastle and Bournemouth fail to beat Crystal Palace.



“We’ve given ourselves a great chance,” Carrick said.

“We’ve put ourselves in a big position. I think these last two results have been big to that.

“It’s a tough league, I think you can see that throughout the league, so to get the amount of wins we’ve had and especially after the setbacks.

“The Newcastle defeat to then bounce back with (beating) Villa. The Leeds one to bounce back again.

“I think the lads have got to take a bit of credit for that because this week’s been very effective in terms of the league.

“So the other side of it is the Champions League is one thing, but it’s not something that we should be over celebrating, either.

“We want to be finishing high up the league really and we want to be challenging high up the league and trying to get more points.

“It’s one thing certainly we need to try and achieve it and we’ve put ourselves in a good position at this moment.



“But there’s still more work to be done.”

Carrick also claimed Bruno Fernandes “deserved” to be named the player of the year.

Fernandes tallied his 19th Premier League assist of the season for Benjamin Sesko’s winning goal against Brentford and Fernandes is one shy of Kevin de Bruyne and Thierry Henry’s record of 20.

Carrick has been reluctant to talk up Fernandes’ chances as he is wary of portraying United as a one-man team.

But when asked if Fernandes merited the end-of-season awards, Carrick replied: “Hopefully he does. He deserves it.



“For the impact that he’s had and the moments that he’s created. I think, whether that’s creating, whether that’s scoring. How his influence within the group is.

“He’s had a big season. There’s no getting away from it.

“And it was another good performance for him tonight.”

Sports.title: How Arsenal’s ‘double press’ trap will exploit Atletico Madrid’s Champions League weakness
Sports.content:
ARSENAL will be looking to move one step closer to their first Champions League title on Wednesday when they face Atletico Madrid in the first leg of the semi-finals.

And they can go into the clash with some confidence off the back of their 1-0 win over Newcastle at the weekend – even if it wasn’t the most convincing result or performance.





That’s because the Premier League meeting can be treated as a blueprint for the upcoming visit to Madrid.

Following a dip in form, the Gunners showed some encouraging signs at the Emirates on Saturday.

And the return of star man Bukayo Saka proved to be a big advantage.

In the Tactics Exposed studio this week, Will Pugh spoke to Dean Scoggins about how the likes of Saka and Eberechi Eze can unlock the Atletico defence.



BACK, SAK & CRACK

The return of Saka saw the reintroduction of Arsenal‘s effective triangle shape on the right side.

That will be hugely beneficial against Atletico because that is where much of the space will be.



Dean said: “Bukayo Saka is back and the Arsenal shape is back. It was a perfect dress rehearsal because Newcastle’s big, physical press is exactly what we expect from Atletico Madrid.

“That right-side triangle we used to talk about all the time? It’s returned.

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“We saw Ben White, Saka and Martin Odegaard forming that shape that had gone missing while Odegaard was injured and Arteta experimented with a few different players.

“That is going to be massive against Atletico because of the way they set up.

“Diego Simeone doesn’t just park the bus anymore. They’ve conceded 26 goals in 13 games – two a game.



“They play a bizarre system where Giuliano Simeone plays the right side almost on his own, like a wing-back.

“They play very tight and narrow. Arsenal should not bother attacking down the left because it will be too crowded in that area.

“The Gunners didn’t even try it against Newcastle; the attack zones show they heavily favoured that right side.

“Atletico Madrid also encourage the left-back to ‘jump’ out of position to hit the winger hard.



“Because the rest of their back five stays so tight, it leaves a huge area of space between the left centre-back and the left-back.

“That is the space for Arsenal to exploit. Take the left-back for a run out of that position and get somebody else to run through the inside – that could be Odegaard or Gyokeres.

“Off the ball, Arsenal can set a trap. Against Newcastle, Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi played as a double pivot, which allows the front four to go on a ‘double press’ – two players coming narrow along with the striker to close the ball down.

“Barcelona showed the way against Atleti. You force them into midfield where they only have two bodies and then hit them again. If you win it there, you’ve caught them in a 5-2-3 transition with no cover.

“If you force them to go long, you’re winning. They will have Antoine Griezmann or Ademola Lookman up top but neither is an aerial threat against William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes.



EB & FLOW

Following a slow start to life in North London, Eze has provided a much-needed spark in the Arsenal attack.

His ability to come inside from the left and partner Odegaard in that attacking midfield position could unlock the Atletico backline and create some major goalscoring opportunities.

Dean said: “Eze is going to be the secret weapon in that transition. People worry about his lack of touches — just 19 against Newcastle — but he was told to stay inside and link play between the lines.

“In that 4-2-4 press, if Rice wins the second ball, Eze is the first pass in the hole. Atletico leave a massive gap in front of their back five, and that is where Eze will do the damage.”



IN THE RED CORNER

Arsenal could also punish Atletico Madrid with one of their biggest strengths – set-pieces.

That strength also seems to be a big weakness for the Spanish side right now, which will be music to the ears of Gabriel and Saliba.



Dean added: “Atletico have been incredibly vulnerable when defending set-pieces lately.

“Five of the last seven goals they’ve conceded have been from set-pieces or crosses. They don’t attack the ball well and they aren’t aggressive in the leap.

“We saw short corners against Newcastle to lure defenders out, but I expect the traditional delivery in Madrid.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Atletico try to push the line out to the penalty spot to give the goalkeeper enough space, but it leaves the back post totally empty. Gabriel will be looking at that.

“Whether it’s an in-swinger or an out-swinger, Atletico Madrid defenders like Clement Lenglet and Robin Le Normand are not going to enjoy Saliba, Gabriel and Gyokeres charging at them. Expect plenty of action in that six-yard box.”

Sports.title: Kobbie Mainoo celebrates proposed new deal with amazing display vs Brentford but Amad wasteful
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED moved within a whisker of qualifying for the Champions League after a nervy 2-1 win over Brentford.

First half goals from Casemiro and Benjamin Sesko saw United strengthen their hold on third in the Premier League table.



Mathias Jensen’s late sweet strike created late anxiety, but Michael Carrick gave his job bid an extra boost after moving three points above Aston Villa and next opponents Liverpool.



And United won a game with a back-three after Carrick replaced Amad at the break, while Bees striker Igor Thiago squandered several chances.

United skipper Bruno Fernandes moved within one assist of matching Thierry Henry and Kevin de Bruyne’s season record of 20.

Here is how SunSport’s Katherine Walsh rated and slated the players from United’s 14th night game of the season.

Senne Lammens – 8

The Belgian was United’s best player in the first half after a great save kept Michael Kayode out from point-blank range shortly after the hosts went ahead.

He followed it up with two massive stops before Sesko doubled the lead on the stroke of half-time. Dealt well with crowding in the box but couldn’t manage a second successive clean sheet for the first time.

Diogo Dalot – 6

Brentford exploited the space between Dalot and Maguire and kept coming down the Portugal international’s side for any luck.

He improved after the break after leaving the defence exposed early on.



Harry Maguire – 6

A welcome return to the starting XI after his two-game ban. Maguire’s set piece strength should sent shockwaves to England boss Thomas Tuchel.

He headed across a corner to assist Casemiro’s opener, minutes after having a chance clawed inches off the line by Caoimhin Kelleher. The Bees stopper saved another straight after the break.

Ayden Heaven – 6

Kept in the lineup following his strong maiden start under Carrick against Chelsea and performed well enough, but perhaps a tad fortunate to avoid giving a penalty away when his arm blocked a cross heading towards Thiago.

Saved his centre-back partner when Maguire was robbed of the ball inside his own area. Has played a considerable role in United’s best week in recent memory.



Luke Shaw – 6

Endured a poor start when he was booked inside five minutes for a pull back following a bleak cross that stinted United’s momentum.

A real mixed bag. Had some decent defensive interventions but was lacking in forward areas. Went off with 15 minutes to go with injury or illness.

Casemiro – 7

This is some farewell tour the Brazil captain is having. His back-post header in the 11th minute was his ninth goal of the campaign.

Despite his goal, the 34-year-old had his work cut out against Brentford’s technical midfield, but he came came close to a third goal in the latter stages. Headed everything clear when United were under the cosh.



Kobbie Mainoo – 8

Mainoo is on the verge of signing fresh terms and celebrated with an epic dribble into the box only for Amad to have hit shot blocked.

Was more assured in his defensive duties, won most of his duels and stepped up a gear in ball carrying. A really strong showing.

Bruno Fernandes – 7

United’s engine room is just two assists away from Premier League history and four games away from becoming the first United star to win player of the season since Wayne Rooney in 2010.



The skipper lead by example and covered every blade of grass after a galvanising team huddle pre-match and several world-class switches of play.

Bryan Mbeumo – 6

Mbeumo has improved in form since his benching against Leeds and followed up a strong Chelsea showing by working hard against his former club.

Amad – 5

In a first start as a left-winger, Amad fluffed a big chance that Matheus Cunha would have perhaps scored had he not been injured.

He was then caught miles offside as his goal was chalked off, which would have been United’s second. The Ivory Coast was subbed off for Noussair Mazraoui at half-time.



Benjamin Sesko – 6

Was more assured tonight and smashed home a second goal of the evening for his 11th of the campaign.

Held his run superbly and showed real striker’s instincts to find the space. Sesko is growing in confidence in a United shirt.

SUBS

Noussair Mazraoui (for Amad, 46) – 6

Unfortnate to miss out on the XI after a heroic display as a makeshift centre-half at Chelsea. He was solid again in his 45 minutes.

Leny Yoro (Shaw, 73) – 6

Did not do too much wrong on his first return since his hip injury ruled him out of the trip to Stamford Bridge.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mason Mount (for Mbeumo, 74) – 5

A few clever touches as he works his way back to full fitness.

Joshua Zirkzee (for Sesko, 87) – N/A

Hardly shored things up when he came on and looked way off it.

Sports.title: Man Utd 2 Brentford 1: Bruno Fernandes nears all-time Premier League record as fans do best to convince him to stay
Sports.content:
THIS COULD well be Manchester United’s best week in years, never mind the season.

A win at the start of the week is likely to end with Champions League qualification mathematically secured.





The absence of a midweek match may well be filled by the announcement of a new deal for Kobbie Mainoo that is all but announced.

Bruno Fernandes is also closing in on another record.

Fernandes tallied his 19th Premier League assist of this career-best season of his. He is now one shy of the joint record held by Kevin De Bruyne and Thierry Henry with four games remaining.

United are practically campaigning for Fernandes during awards season and it was his name the crowd chanted even when Benjamin Sesko got the goal.

A little bit of extra love will do no harm in convincing Fernandes to continue playing at Old Trafford next season.

His future is now effectively moot with United due to have their name in the pot for next season’s Champions League draw.

In another barren season at Old Trafford, Fernandes could clinch his own treble: the PFA and FWA trophies may have a new home alongside the Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year statue.

United’s flattering win against Brentford was a good gauge of where they are at.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

United enjoyed their best start to a game under Michael Carrick since his first match back in charge yet they have seldom looked so porous.

Igor Thiago started the night three goals behind Erling Haaland for the Premier League Golden Boot and had enough chances to go level with the Manchester City striker.

Fernandes is the talk of the town at United but Senne Lammens was as much of a matchwinner.



The Belgian made three vital saves with United only 1-0 up.

Carrick demanded calmness from United at a goal kick amid Brentford’s dominance and even resorted to a defensive change and formation switch at the interval.

Brentford, victors over United in the reverse fixture in September, lacked the ruthlessness that United exhibited in their penalty area at the start and end of the first half.

The United team leaked before kick-off but the defence was leakier. Carrick initiated a second-half lockdown to record his ninth win from 13 games.

United initially promised a more handsome win and their best spell was the 11 minutes before Casemiro changed the scoreboard.



Mainoo, who has agreed a new five-year contract, embarked on a dribble beyond most playmakers to tee up Amad in the third minute but the left-footer’s right-footed strike bounced off Sepp van den Berg.

That set the tone for both players’ performances.



Carrick felt Mainoo’s performance in the 1-0 win at Chelsea was his best during his three-month tenure and this was another complete midfield display.

Mainoo was more comfortable mucking in than Casemiro, whose goals have masked his relative ineffectiveness in a defensive capacity.

Caoimhin Kelleher parried a Harry Maguire header away from a corner and Maguire met another dead-ball kick to assist Casemiro, ghosting in at the far post.

Casemiro’s ninth goal take him above playmakers Fernandes and Matheus Cunha in United’s scoring charts.

United fans gullibly sang “One more year, Casemiro” again as he kissed the badge.



That sparked one-way traffic – from Brentford.

United all but stopped playing after Casemiro milked the adoration and the Brentford analysts in the press box were at a loss that their side had not scored.

Thiago failed to anticipate Luke Shaw’s airshot at the far post and Lammens spread himself to block the unmarked Michael Kayode from close range.

Thiago passed on shooting when played in, spooked by Diogo Dalot.



He breached United again only to be thwarted by Lammens.

The haphazard Ayden Heaven almost guided the ball into his own net with his arm.

That drew the most eye-catching stop from Lammens.

United had fired a shot across Brentford’s bows on the breakaway when Amad converted but was so far offside he was in a different timezone.

They timed their next counter perfectly, with Fernandes maximising the three-on-two to charge into the Brentford area and slip the ball to Sesko, who waited for the retreating Nathan Collins to commit before lashing in.



Lammens charged out of his goal to celebrate with team-mates.

He merited the congratulations as much as Sesko, having kept United’s sheet clean in a misleading half.

Sesko opted for his new trademark ‘jump’ celebration, a homage to Michael Jordan.

The Slovenian is now United’s outright top scorer with 11 goals.



It was the first time Amad had ever started on the left wing and the experiment lasted a half.

Carrick was so dissatisfied he replaced him with full back Noussair Mazraoui and United switched to a back three, the first time they had shifted to that system since Ruben Amorim’s contract was shredded in January.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

United kept Brentford at bay until Dango Ouattara flicked the ball against the crossbar from a corner and threatened to acrobatically decapitate Harry Maguire on the rebound.

Mathias Jensen eventually broke the stoic United rear-guard with a thunderous strike from range, but it proved to be nothing more than a consolation.

Sports.title: Luke Shaw hands Man Utd and England injury scare just weeks before World Cup as he is forced off against Brentford
Sports.content:
ENGLAND have been dealt another late World Cup scare after Luke Shaw was subbed off for Manchester United against Brentford.

The left-back, who has started every Premier League game this season, was replaced by Leny Yoro with just under 20 minutes left of Monday’s win.





He was treated by a physio before walking from the pitch slowly, although without assistance.

Shaw, 30, spoke to medics as he sat on the grass in front of his team’s goal for the second half.

He did so through his shirt so as not to be easily lip read having gone down despite no clear impact or incident.

Shaw is yet to make a squad under Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel since he took over the team.



But his form for United has made him one of a number of players competing for a spot in the 26-man playing group later this year.

Ahead of naming the squad for last month’s friendlies against Uruguay and Japan, Tuchel said when asked about Shaw’s omission: “These tough decisions come with the job.”

However, another comment he made, suggesting that camp was the “Last chance to get to know new players” suggests it may already be too late for the former Southampton defender.

In August, Tuchel had left the door open for Shaw, saying: “It was a very close call.

“I just want him to have a little bit more minutes. He looks very fit, he looks very determined.

“I think he has the quality, the experience to play for and to make us better straight away.

“But I want to keep him back a little bit, when he has more rhythm than he has right now.”

Shaw has managed to do that but has not made the cut so far under German Tuchel.

Instead, Tino Livramento, Lewis Hall, Miles Lewis-Skelley, and now Nico O’Reilly have all staked a claim.



Shaw’s last appearance for his country was in the Euro 2024 final against Spain.

He was a favourite under Gareth Southgate despite the fitness issues that had plagued his previous couple of years.

Tuchel has already had to see Harry Kane, Bukayo Saka, Livramento, and Cole Palmer all continue with knocks of their own in recent weeks.

Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite, an outsider, has been ruled out of contention due a hamstring injury.

Sports.title: Man City make special request to Premier League in bid to boost title charge against Arsenal
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER CITY have asked for the Premier League to help ease their fixture pile up in the final two weeks of the season.

Pep Guardiola’s FA Cup finalists could have to play three games in six or seven days as they chase a domestic treble next month.





However their rivals do not believe City should be given any special treatment and talks were still ongoing last night (Sunday).

The Etihad giants have to find new dates for two Prem fixtures due to their success in the domestic cups.

Their home game against Crystal Palace was postponed due to the Carabao Cup final and the trip to Bournemouth was scheduled for FA Cup final weekend.

Prem rules say they should be played in the order they were called off – but one option explored is for the two to be reversed.

It seems unlikely other clubs will agree to bending the rules – meaning they will tackle the Eagles on May 13, then play the FA Cup final the following Saturday.

The trip to the Vitality would most likely be on Tuesday, May 19 – as Uefa will not want it clashing with the Europa League final the following night.

However until anything is confirmed, City will continue to fight their case.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

They are currently three points behind Arsenal with a game in hand after the weekend’s action.



Mikel Arteta‘s side beat Newcastle 1-0 at the Emirates on Saturday to move back into the lead but could not substantially increase their goal difference.

Arsenal will be six clear at the summit before City next play if they win at home to Fulham on Saturday, May 2.

That comes after they travel to Madrid to face Atletico on Wednesday night in the Champions League.

City have a longer break as they prepare to go to Everton on Monday, May 4.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez spotted in Madrid just weeks after flirting with transfer exit from Chelsea
Sports.content:
ENZO FERNANDEZ has been photographed in Madrid – just weeks after entertaining a move to LaLiga giants Real.

The Chelsea midfielder controversially opened the door to a future move to the Bernabeu earlier this month by saying: “I’d like to live in Madrid.





“It’s a beautiful city, reminds me of Buenos Aires.”

Fernandez’s flirting with a move to Madrid saw the club slap him with a two-match suspension, but that hasn’t stopped him from travelling to the Spanish capital.

Less than 24 hours after sealing Chelsea’s place in the FA Cup final last Sunday, Fernandez was spotted taking in the Mutua Madrid Open.



Paps also spotted the tennis super-fan in the streets of Madrid with team-mates Marc Cucurella and Joao Pedro.

Interim boss Calum McFarlane gave the Blues time off after their 1-0 win over Leeds.

Fernandez booked the west Londoners a place in the final with a 23rd-minute header.

McFarlane was full of praise for the Argentina international after the match, saying: “He’s a winner.



“He’s got so much talent, he’s got so much fight, he’s massive for this group.

“And the best thing about Enzo is that he can do a bit of everything.

“But when it gets tough, you see the fight in him, you see him driving the group on, you see him making tackles, you see him fighting for every loose ball.

“So he was exceptional today and deserved his Man of the Match.



“In terms of making Enzo Fernandez captain, I’m very aware that I’m the interim coach, and Enzo is the vice-captain of this club, so I wasn’t hesitant to make him captain, now that Reece James isn’t fit to play this game.

“I said that to him at the end, I said, ‘You like scoring at the back post for me’.

Sports.title: Harry Maguire makes feelings clear on Michael Carrick's major change at Man Utd
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire makes feelings clear on Michael Carrick's major change at Man Utd

Manchester United are just one point away from securing a return to the Champions League as their fine form under Michael Carrick continued courtesy of a 2-1 win over Brentford

View 2 Images Harry Maguire feels Manchester United have improved significantly since changing shape to a back four (Image: Sky Sports)

Harry Maguire spoke of how Manchester United's players feel more comfortable playing in a back four after they all but secured their return to Champions League football under Michael Carrick.

‌



The Red Devils' fortunes have been transformed since Carrick was handed the reigns on an interim basis back in January after the club parted company with Ruben Amorim. Monday night's 2-1 win over Brentford, Carrick's ninth victory in 13 games, means United need just one points from their final four games to guarantee a top-five finish.

‌



Amorim heavily favoured a back three formation during his turbulent reign at Old Trafford and was scrutinised for refusing to be flexible in his approach. United's improvements have coincided with a formation change under Carrick, though the 44-year-old did change shape at half-time in a bid to tighten United's grip on the game.

‌



Maguire was superb in both boxes for United with his header setting up Casemiro for the game's opening goal after 11 minutes.

Man Utd survive Brentford scare and move step closer to Champions League - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Man Utd injury blow as Luke Shaw goes off during Brentford clash READ MORE :

But the England defender was quick to talk up the benefits of playing in a back four when he was asked if some players were more comfortable playing in a back three after Amorim's spell. He told Sky Sports in response: "No, definitely not. I think the formation change has helped us a lot to be honest. I think the results spoke for itself.

"Michael come in and changed to a back four and the results have picked up a lot now. I think we're comfortable that we can play both formations, but yeah, we didn't cover the pitch well enough in the last 20 minutes of the first half and were letting too many balls into the box.

‌



"They had a lot of chances in the last 20 minutes of the first half. I think it was good that the manager recognised that and changed [it] for the second half and we were a lot more comfortable."

View 2 Images Casemiro and Benjamin Sesko scored the all-important goals for Manchester United (Image: Darren Staples/AFP)

When he was asked to discuss the impact that Carrick has had, including the much talk about change of shape, Maguire lauded United's interim head coach.

‌



"The results helped the feeling massively," he said. "We had two tough fixtures when Michael came in [against Arsenal and Man City] and I think everyone was probably looking at them thinking, 'Oh no'. We managed to get six points and from then on everyone has believed in it and we've got confidence.

"I think we can still get a lot better in this formation as well. As a back four we can slide across the pitch a lot quicker, like we should have done in the first half today, but we will get better the longer we work as a unit in there.

"But the results speak for themselves since the manager has come in and the formation has changed. We just seem to pick up results. I think the games previous, when Ruben was here, a lot of the games were 50-50 but we always ended up on the back of a defeat. Now it feels like it's the other way round where we're a lot better in both boxes; we defend our box a lot better and we're managing to be clinical in the other box."

Sports.title: Man Utd on brink of Champions League return as brilliant Casemiro shines again
Sports.content:
Man Utd on brink of Champions League return as brilliant Casemiro shines again

MAN UTD 2-1: BRENTFORD Goals from Casemiro and Benjamin Sesko were enough to consolidate the Red Devils' grip on third place with qualification for the Champions League in sight

View 3 Images Casemiro celebrates after scoring Manchester United's opening goal against Brentford (Image: Darren Staples/AFP)

Casemiro served up another helping of Brazilian brilliance, to help move Manchester United a step closer to the top table of European football.

‌



The veteran midfielder might be leaving Old Trafford in a few weeks time, but will do so with a bang after his first half header sent United towards a crucial 2-0 win.

‌



Benjamin Sesko added a second as United put significant breathing space between themselves and their closest rivals in the scrap for Champions League qualification, while putting a dent in Brentford's own hopes of European football next season.

‌



Mathias Jensen had pulled one back with three minutes of normal time remaining, but it wasn't enough as United held on.

Man Utd injury blow as Luke Shaw goes off during Brentford clash READ MORE :

Man Utd survive Brentford scare and move step closer to Champions League - 5 talking points READ MORE :

There is never a game which doesn't involve huge pressure, when it comes to United. And the home side knew a win here would move them three points clear of Liverpool and Aston Villa - and into the driving seat when it came to Champions League qualification.

But Brentford came to town with European designs of their own: three points for Keith Andrews' men would see them leapfrog Chelsea, Bournemouth and Brighton into sixth place - and throw a real spanner in the works.

‌



Carrick was boosted by the return of Harry Maguire from suspension, but had to cope without the injured Matheus Cunha, due to a sore hip.

United made a blistering start and should have been ahead inside two minutes. Kobbie Mainoo turned into Diego Maradona for a moment, with a sensational run that saw him go past three defenders before teeing up Amad Diallo. It seemed impossible not to score, with Caoimhin Kelleher stranded by Mainoo's brilliance, but somehow Sepp van den Berg got back to deflect Diallo's shot wide.

View 3 Images Benjamin Sesko scored United's second after some more Bruno Fernandes brilliance (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

‌



But United were brimming with confidence and laid seige to the Brentford goal. It took a stunning save from Kelleher to keep out Maguire's header millimetres before it crossed the line. While a sublime pass from Bruno Fernandes sent Bryan Mbeumo racing clear, only for Brentford to scramble back and snuff out the danger.

But United got the breakthrough they deserved on 12 minutes when Casemiro stole in at the back post to meet Maguire's headed cross and plant one of his own into the back of the goal.

Brentford could have equalised when Keane Lewis-Potter's cross almost picked out Igor Thiago, but Luke Shaw managed to ride to the rescue with a desperate intervention.

‌



Senne Lammens then somehow managed to deny Michael Kayode from almost point blank range.

View 3 Images Casemiro's looping header broke the deadlock (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

It was fast, furious and fantastic in equal measure. So much so that Thiago could have had a hat-trick in the same amount of minutes. He lost his footing and the ball with just Lammens to beat, then saw another effort superbly saved by the United goalkeeper. Seconds later he was cursing Lammens again, when he flung himself to his right to tip wide another goal bound strike from the wasteful Brazilian.

‌



United were walking a tightrope. But they made Brentford pay before half time when Feranndes charged forward and put a chance on a plate for Sesko, who duly doubled United's lead.

It was Fernandes's 19th assist of the season, leaving him one short of the Premier League record.

It was also a painful blow to a Brentford side which should have been ahead themselves.

Article continues below

Jensen's dripping drive offered them so hope, but the visitors were left to regret being so shocking in front of goal on a night of sheer frustration for Andrews.

Sports.title: Man Utd survive Brentford scare and move step closer to Champions League - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Man Utd survive Brentford scare and move step closer to Champions League - 5 talking points

MAN UTD 2-1 BRENTFORD: Michael Carrick's side made it back-to-back wins courtest of goals from Casemiro and Benjamin Sesko, although they had to survive a late scare

View 5 Images Benjamin Sesko was back on the scoresheet (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

Manchester United edged closer to sealing Champions League qualification by beating misfiring Brentford 2-1. Goals from Casemiro and Benjamin Sesko gave Michael Carrick his ninth win as United's interim manager, a position he's increasingly likely to remain in next season.

‌



But Keith Andrews will be ruing his team's poor finishing which let a rudderless home defence off the hook. Thiago missed a slew of chances in what proved to be emblematic of the Bees' problems before an long-range strike from Mathias Jensen made it a nervy finish.

‌



Brentford came into this game six unbeaten while United had returned to winning ways at Chelsea nine days ago. Carrick notably had Harry Maguire back from suspension, easing the Red Devils' injury crisis.

‌



Here are five talking points from Old Trafford.

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

Why Man Utd are wearing a different sponsor in Brentford Premier League clash READ MORE :

1. Carrick dealt double injury blow

Although Maguire was available against, Carrick couldn't call on Matheus Cunha after he scored the winner against Chelsea. The forward had picked up an injury and was replaced in the starting line-up by Amad.

‌



"He just had a bit of a sore hip flexor after the Chelsea game," Carrick told MUTV post-match. "It looked promising in the week but he didn’t recover in time, as hoped. It's nothing too serious but, unfortunately, he misses out tonight."

And in the second half, Luke Shaw had to be hauled off. The England international has started every Premier League game this season, but he's now at risk missing Sunday's clash with Liverpool which can secure Champions League qualification.

Should Manchester United plead with Casemiro to stay? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 5 Images Michael Carrick was without last weekend's match winner (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

2. One more year, one more Casemiro?

With his ninth goal of the season, Casemiro briefly became United's joint-top goalscorer. Who'd have thought that when the Red Devils signed three forwards last summer?

The 34-year-old popped up again to score from a set piece and give Carrick's side an early lead shortly after Amad missed a sitter. Casemiro may be on the decline physically, but United are sure to miss his goals next season - unless he and Sir Jim Ratcliffe listen to what the fans are chanting.

‌



View 5 Images Casemiro got on the end of yet another set piece (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

3. A tale of two strikers

Just as an end-to-end first half was nearing its conclusion, United hit Brentford with Slovenian sucker punch. Sesko, who overtook Casemiro to return to the top of United's scoring chart, made it 10 Premier League goals for the campaign with a ruthless finish after good work from Bruno Fernandes.

If only Thiago could've had the same composure. With United's defence constantly wide open, Brentford's talisman had three golden opportunities to score in the first half, yet he didn't even manage to register a shot.

‌



Whether it be a slippery surface, a mistimed run, Ayden Heaven's arm - deemed not to be a penalty by VAR - or Senne Lammens' saves, Thiago somehow couldn't add to his tally of 21. His failures in front of goal felt especially costly after Sesko scored, coverting his first shot of the night.

View 5 Images Thiago didn't bring his shooting boots to Old Trafford (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

4. Carrick takes a leaf from Amorim's book

Wing-backs looked to be a thing of the past at Old Trafford after the sacking of Ruben Amorim, but Carrick gave a nod to his predecessor with a half-time alteration. Off went Amad and on came Noussair Mazraoui, making it a back five for United.

‌



Amad had looked to be moving freely before the break. But the bulk of Brentford's threat had come down the Bees' right-hand side, so perhaps it was a tactical decision from Carrick to tighten things up in the second half.

5. Brentford's European dream takes a hit

View 5 Images Brentford could've gone sixth with a win (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

The race for Europe is wide open as we enter the run-in, with just four points separating sixth and 12th place in a very tight Premier League. That's why this result will sting even more for the Bees, as they missed the opportunity to take the lead in said race.

Article continues below

Jensen's goal from distance was nothing short of what Brentford deserved, but it proved to be too little too late as their pushed for a draw late on. Saturday's match at home to West Ham is imperative if they want to regain some momentum, having lost for the first time in seven here.
